1.title: W1 · Generic Stack<T>

hardens.title: peek_mut
hardens.note:
Extends W1. Add peek_mut(&mut self) -> Option<&mut T> that returns a mutable reference to the top without popping.
      
Why this hardens you: Forces &mut vs & discipline on the same structure.

hardens.title: Borrowing iterators
hardens.note:
Extends W1. Implement iter(&self) and iter_mut(&mut self) yielding references in top-to-bottom or bottom-to-top order (pick one and document it).
      
Why this hardens you: Same skill as std collections: expose contents without moving.

hardens.title: IntoIterator for references
hardens.note:
Extends W1. Impl IntoIterator for &Stack<T> and &mut Stack<T> so for x in &stack works.

hardens.title: drain
hardens.note:
Extends W1. Add drain(&mut self) -> impl Iterator<Item = T> that empties the stack, yielding owned values. Partial drain + Drop of the iterator must not leak/double-pop wrongly.
      
Why this hardens you: Ownership + partial consumption; classic collection edge.

hardens.title: FromIterator + Extend
hardens.note:
Extends W1. Impl FromIterator<T> and Extend<T> for Stack<T>.
      
Why this hardens you: Build/extend stacks the way std APIs expect.

2.title: W2 · Thread-Safe Counter

hardens.title: CAS: increment if < max
hardens.note:
Extends W2. Using only compare_exchange (no fetch_add), implement try_inc_if_lt(max) -> bool that increments iff current < max.
      
Why this hardens you: Real atomic pattern beyond fetch_add.

hardens.title: Ordering with a flag
hardens.note:
Extends W2. Thread A stores data then sets ready = true. Thread B waits until ready then reads data. Wire orderings so B cannot see ready without seeing data. Explain why Relaxed on both is wrong.
      
Why this hardens you: The W2 senior signal: when Relaxed is insufficient.

hardens.title: Mutex multi-field update
hardens.note:
Extends W2. Maintain { count: u64, last_thread: usize } updated together on each increment. Do it under one mutex (not two atomics).
      
Why this hardens you: When atomics stop being enough — W2 production judgment.

hardens.title: Join-inside-spawn bugfix
hardens.note:
Extends W2. Here is a broken pattern: joining inside the spawn loop serializes threads. Rewrite so all 10 threads run concurrently, then join.
      
Why this hardens you: Concurrency structure, not API trivia.

hardens.title: CAS fetch_max
hardens.note:
Extends W2. Implement fetch_max(a: &AtomicU64, x: u64) -> u64 (previous value) using a CAS loop.
      
Why this hardens you: Composes compare_exchange into a useful primitive.
